old: (Thinking:) 'A heel-seizer, a reinforcer, a middle or a neutral king who would give shelter (to the enemy) or destroy what has been achieved has to be countered; a narrow road has to be cleared; the treasury, the army, the forces of the ally, the enemy or the forest tribes, or the season for labourers, have to be waited for; the exhaustion of the fort-works, stores and defences the enemy has made, the despondency of his hired troops and of his ally's troops will come about; or the instigators (planted in the enemy's camp) are not urging haste; or the enemy will himself fulfil (our) intended purpose' — he should march slowly; in the opposite case, quickly.

new: The clauses up to iti are the considerations for marching slowly. viṣṭi-ṛtu: the season when forced labour (viṣṭi) is available; alternatively 'the season of labour'. upajapitāraḥ: agents who sow dissension among the enemy; na-atitvarayanti could also be read 'are not in too great a hurry'. why: reviewer (minor): The text has pārṣṇi (the heel) alone, glossed with the glossary term 'heel-seizer' (pārṣṇi-grāha); say so in the note.
